newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU vets P&0, Stena Channel ferry venture.
newsitem.headline: EU vets P&0, Stena Channel ferry venture.

text.p: The European Commission sought comments on Friday about a proposal by ferry operators P&O of Britain and Stena Line Ltd to pool forces in the English Channel.

It said the deal was submitted for clearance on October 31 under article 85 of the EU treaty which bans restrictive practices. Alternatively, the two partners asked the Commission to grant them an exemption under the same competition rules.

Peninsular and Oriental Steam Navigation Company (P&O) and Sweden's Stena announced in October they were combining their ferry operations on the English Channel in an offensive against the Eurotunnel.

In defence of their joint plan, the former rivals told the Commission that without the joint venture they were unlikely to provide "sustainable, effective competition in the future" because of Eurotunnnel's "exceptional level of market power", the notice said.
"They consider that there is a foreseeable risk that they will be forced either to scale down their operations in the market(s) concerned or exit the market(s) altogether," the notice said.
The Commission said it had, at this stage, not formed any view on the applicability of article 85 to the agreement. It called on interested parties to comment within a month.

The two companies have agreed to pool their respective ferry operations on the English Channel and between Dover and the Belgian port of Zeebrugge, on the North Sea, in a joint venture called P&O Stena Line.

The new service is expected to operate a regular service between Dover and Calais, by far the busiest route, departing every 45 minutes and employing six vessels for both tourist and freight services.
There is no deadline for the Commission to give its final verdict.
